newsitem.title: CHINA: China, U.S. begin textile talks in Beijing.
newsitem.headline: China, U.S. begin textile talks in Beijing.

text.p: Washington's top textile negotiator Rita Hayes on Monday began talks in Beijing aimed at ending a dispute over U.S. penalties on Chinese textile imports, U.S. officials said.

Hayes, textile negotiator of the U.S. Trade Representative Office, would also discuss a new Sino-U.S textile agreement during talks with China's Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation, an official of the U.S. embassy said.
"The talks started this morning," he said. "We expect them to last four days."
The United States set penalties of $19 million on Chinese imports in September, saying Beijing was shipping textiles through third countries to avoid quota restrictions.
China has threatened to retaliate by temporarily banning imports of some U.S. textiles, farm goods and alcoholic drinks, with the curbs to go into effect on December 10.
The two sides also must agree to extend textile cooperation by concluding a new agreement to replace the current textile pact that expires at the end of the year, officials say.
China's huge textile sales to the United States have long been a sensitive point for U.S. trade negotiators eager to reduce their country's swelling trade deficit.

Washington says its 1995 trade deficit with China was worth $35 billion, making trade a major issue in ties already strained by disagreement over Taiwan, weapons sales, nuclear proliferation and copyright piracy.
